title: Streaming fixture harness and retry simulation for SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a deterministic fixture harness for streaming endpoints (text generation streaming, token-level events, and structured streaming) that can simulate partial responses, transient errors, and retry scenarios across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. The harness will be used by unit, integration, and contract tests to validate SDK streaming ergonomics (resume/reconnect, backpressure handling, cancelation), retry semantics (idempotency, duplication, out-of-order chunks), and example apps. Goal is a single, extensible mock-server fixture format that CI can run to assert contract stability and prevent regressions in the SDKs and runtime client behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A mock-server fixture format (JSON) that expresses a deterministic sequence of stream events, delays, mid-stream injection of HTTP errors (e.g., 502), and reconnect expectations
SDK test harnesses (Python/TS/Go) can consume fixtures and assert library-level behaviors: resume logic, on_message ordering, and correct emission of partial/incremental tokens
CI integration: a contract test job that runs fixtures against the hosted Redwood API and the mock harness to validate parity for streaming semantics
Clear examples and docs in the SDK repos showing how to record a streaming cassette, replay with deterministic timing, and write a new contract test
implementation_notes: Design a compact fixture schema that lists: initial HTTP handshake, sequence of stream frames (data/metadata/heartbeat), per-frame delays in milliseconds, optional chunk corruption flags, and explicit 'expected-client-behavior' assertions (e.g., must-ack, reconnect-with-token). Implement a standalone Node-based mock server (lightweight) that can operate in two modes: replay-from-fixture and live-proxy-with-cassette (record). The replay mode must support both chunked HTTP and SSE/WebSocket emulation so we can test different SDK transports. Add helper CLI to convert recorded network captures into canonical fixtures and to fuzz timing for flakiness detection. Ensure deterministic RNG seed parameter for time-freeze/replay fuzzing. Keep fixture files small and human-readable so engineers can author tests quickly.
testing_plan: Phase 1: Prototype Node mock server + simple fixture format and run local Python SDK unit tests to validate parsing and event ordering
Phase 2: Extend fixtures to simulate mid-stream 502/timeout and implement reconnect token semantics; add equivalent tests for TypeScript and Go SDKs
Phase 3: Add 'record' mode to capture live Redwood API streaming sessions into fixtures; sanity-check parity by replaying recorded fixtures against the real API in a nightly job
Phase 4: Add CI contract job (runs on merge for SDK repos) which runs a representative subset of fixtures against mock server and against canary Redwood endpoint to detect regressions
risks: Recorded network traces may capture non-deterministic timing patterns that are hard to canonicalize
SDK-specific transport differences (sse vs http-chunked vs websocket) could lead to divergent expectations unless the fixture schema is general enough
Maintenance burden if fixtures are too verbose or brittle; require tooling to sanitize and compress common patterns
updates: 2025-02-15 — Created ticket. Spike plan approved by SDK leads (Asha, Liam). Chosen Node-based mock server for fast iteration.

2025-02-21 — Prototype replay engine implemented; verified Python SDK receives tokens in correct order for a basic fixture. Observed that Go SDK's default HTTP client buffers causing different chunk boundaries — added transport shim in Go tests.

2025-02-26 — Added CLI 'recorder' to convert a raw netlog into fixture schema; discovered edge case where server-sent events include multi-line metadata — updated fixture grammar to include message_type field.

2025-03-01 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/mockstream/pull/4 with basic replay server and three example fixtures (simple-gen, reconnect-with-token, duplicated-chunk). Running TS and Go test runs locally; TS client needs small API ergonomics tweak documented in follow-up ENG-31845.
notes: This ticket prioritizes test determinism over feature completeness. We will iterate on the fixture schema after adding 10-15 real-world recordings and feedback from SDK maintainers. Follow-up tickets will cover full CI integration and maintenance tooling (fixture linter, size optimizer).
